question: The national recovery and resilience plan (NRRP) provides for investments for sustainable mobility in inland areas. However, Avellino railway station, a strategic node for Irpinia, still has no electrification project or timeline for integration with regional and interregional lines.

Local civil society rallied around a petition, ‘Ridateci il treno: stop all'isolamento di Avellino’ (‘Give us back the train: end Avellino's isolation’), which garnered more than 5 000 signatures, and at a well-attended public assembly, ‘Ridateci il treno’, denouncing the area’s isolation, which hampers economic development, university accessibility and the green transition.
A number of institutional representatives have also raised this matter, highlighting the dearth of transparency regarding the timing and monitoring of the works funded. In the light of the above: 1.
Is the Commission aware of the delays to the NRRP measures for sustainable mobility in inland Italy, in particular with regard to the electrification of the railway line serving Avellino?

With a view to preventing EU resources from being wasted or used late, what auditing and monitoring tools does the Commission plan to use to ensure that the timelines and objectives Italy set in the NRRP are met?

Will the Commission check whether inland areas such as Avellino and Borgo Ferrovia are included in sustainable mobility programmes (NRRP Mission 3, SNAI, POR/ERDF) and, if not, call on the Italian authorities to ensure that they are included?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (8.1.2026) The Commission is closely engaged in the monitoring of railway investments and their implementation progress through the assessment of Italy’s payment requests for the completed milestones and targets under the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF). In this regard, the Commission published its preliminary assessment1.

Based on the information available to the Commission, the Avellino project is not among those that Italy intends to report under the RRF payment requests. However, given the performance-based nature of the RRF, Italy has room to include these projects when submitting a payment request considering that for railway projects the performance is measured by the number of km built.

The milestones and targets related to railway investments in Italy are part of payment requests to be submitted by Italy in 2026. Member States remain primarily responsible for the implementation of their recovery and resilience plans as approved by the Council, as well as for verifying that the financing provided has been properly used in accordance with all applicable rules.
